objective.statement: Write the scales and key signature of F sharp major and D sharp minor.
successCriteria: I know both keys have six sharps and are relative to each other.
I spell each scale with every letter name used once, including E sharp and C double sharp.
I place the six sharps in the right order in each clef.

explanation.text: The new keys of Grade 5 have six sharps or six flats. F♯ major has six sharps (F♯ C♯ G♯ D♯ A♯ E♯), and its relative minor, D♯ minor, has the same six. The notes of the F♯ major scale are the same keys on the piano as those of G♭ major; the two keys are enharmonic equivalents, written differently.

music.textAlternative: The scale of F sharp major, ascending, written with accidentals: F♯ G♯ A♯ B C♯ D♯ E♯ F♯.

explanation.caption: F♯ major: six sharps. The seventh note is E♯, not F: each letter is used once.

explanation.text: Spell a scale by letters first: eight notes, each letter name once, from F to F. Then add the sharps the key needs. This is why the leading note is E♯: the letter before F is E, and E♯ is a semitone below F♯. Writing F♮ instead would use F twice and skip E.

music.textAlternative: The harmonic minor scale of D sharp, ascending: D♯ E♯ F♯ G♯ A♯ B C𝄪 D♯.

explanation.caption: D♯ harmonic minor: the raised seventh is C double sharp (C𝄪).

explanation.text: In D♯ minor the harmonic form raises the seventh note, which is already C♯ in the key signature, so it becomes C𝄪 (C double sharp). The melodic form raises the sixth and seventh going up (B♯ and C𝄪) and lowers them again coming down. You will be asked to write scales in the treble or bass clef; you should also know where the six sharps sit in the alto and tenor clefs.
Letters first, accidentals second. The order of sharps in a signature: F C G D A E: F♯ major has all six of them.

music.textAlternative: The first four notes of F sharp major: F♯ G♯ A♯ B.

steps: The key signature sharpens F, G and A, but not B... B stays natural.
So F♯ G♯ A♯ B: a semitone between A♯ and B.
demonstration.textAlternative: F sharp major, first four notes.
